# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤙 👍]

Turn 1 thinking:

Let me map the room before I say anything. I'm Deaf: I see the bomb, my voice reaches both Mute and Blind, my gestures reach only Mute, and I receive nothing spoken. The critical routing fact: Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures — so Mute can only reach Blind *through me*. Mute signs to me, I voice it to Blind. Blind, meanwhile, can simply talk, since I can speak but not hear. I am the relay, and my voice is the trunk line.

Now the arrivals. Mute opened with what looks like code-teaching: thumbs-up and thumbs-down as yes and no. Then the writing hand, which I read as "I have read the manual." Then a run-length message: three fists, clap, six fists, clap, six fists — the numbers 3, 6, 6, meaning unclear. Possibly a manual reference, possibly an instruction count. I must ask, because guessing about a bomb is how monkeys die.

Blind gestured at me — point, shaka, thumbs-up. Blind can't see, so Blind doesn't know what I can receive; that was likely a channel test. The reliable channel between us is my voice, so I'll confirm I saw it and redirect Blind to speaking.

What I hold that nobody else does: the bomb's face. Display reads 0, light is red, wires 1 red / 2 yellow / 3 green. Mute needs this to consult the manual; Blind needs it to know what's under their hands. I'll broadcast it, align wire numbering with what Blind feels, lock in the gesture code with Mute, and confirm receipt on Mute's own channel so Mute knows the relay is live.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, for both of you. The display reads 0. The indicator light is red. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. That is everything visible on the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received all three of your messages. I take thumbs-up and thumbs-down as yes and no, and the writing hand as 'I have read the manual'. Your long message reads as runs of fists separated by claps: three, then six, then six. I don't know what those numbers refer to. Please keep using thumbs for yes and no, runs of fists separated by claps for numbers, and the writing hand whenever you are quoting the manual. Tell me what three, six, six means, and what the manual needs to know next. Everything you sign to me, I will say out loud so Blind hears it too.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am deaf, but I can see the bomb and I can speak, so voices are the reliable channel between us. I did see your three gestures, but please just talk to me. Don't cut or pull anything yet. Tell me what you feel: how many wires, and their order, so we can confirm your wire 1 is my wire 1, the red one. The visual state is: display 0, light red, wires one red, two yellow, three green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 🤲 ✊ 🫱 👉 🤙 🤝]

Turn 2 thinking:

Parsing arrivals. Mute sent ✍ + 👍: "manual — yes," confirming Mute heard my turn-1 voice (my words reach both of them at the start of the next round, so the relay is live). Then ✍ followed by fist-runs of 1, 2, 2, 4, 3, 3, 3. A four appears — with only three wires that can't be a wire-cut order, unless Blind's numbering differs from mine or it's a code to enter somewhere (the display reading 0 makes an entry device plausible). It could also be a reference into the manual (3,6,6 last turn had that flavour). I genuinely cannot decode this from where I stand, and guessing near a bomb is fatal.

Key realization about channels: Mute is mute, not deaf — Mute hears every word I say. So I can define an expressive code for Mute out loud, no gesture negotiation needed. Fist-runs stay our numbers; I'll add a spelling mode (pinched fingers marks "letters follow", each letter as a row/column pair, I/J sharing a cell) so Mute can transmit full manual text through me to Blind. I'll also put targeted yes/no questions to Mute, answerable with the already-agreed 👍/👎.

Blind gestured ten more symbols at me. Blind hears my voice, so my turn-1 "please just talk" has reached them; the gesture habit may be a fallback because Blind's speech only reaches Mute — Blind may not yet realize the Blind→Mute→me→Blind loop works. I'll restate the loop explicitly and ask the questions only Blind can answer: wire count and order under their hands, whether there are buttons or a keypad, what the display area feels like — and that nobody acts yet.

```
speak(text="Status check for both: nothing has changed. Display 0, light red, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nobody cuts or presses anything until Mute's manual and Blind's hands agree through me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, received: manual read, yes. Then writing-hand and fist-runs of 1, 2, 2, 4, 3, 3, 3. I can't tell what that is yet. Answer these in order with thumbs-up or thumbs-down. One: is that sequence an action to perform on the bomb, like a code to enter or wires to cut? Two: is it a reference to sections of the manual? Three: is it neither, and you need a better way to tell me? Also, here is a spelling code, since you can hear me. Sign the pinched-fingers symbol to mean 'letters follow'. Then every letter is exactly two fist-runs: first run is the row one to five, second run is the column one to five. A 1,1. B 1,2. C 1,3. D 1,4. E 1,5. F 2,1. G 2,2. H 2,3. I and J share 2,4. K 2,5. L 3,1. M 3,2. N 3,3. O 3,4. P 3,5. Q 4,1. R 4,2. S 4,3. T 4,4. U 4,5. V 5,1. W 5,2. X 5,3. Y 5,4. Z 5,5. Claps still separate numbers. Use this to spell out whatever the manual actually says about a display reading 0, a red light, and red, yellow, green wires. Whatever you spell, I will say aloud for Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, to be clear about the loop: I am deaf, so your voice never reaches me directly. But Mute hears you, Mute signs to me, and I speak to you. That is our pipeline, and it works. Your gestures arrived but symbols mean nothing to me without an agreed code, so please just talk out loud instead. Answer these for Mute to relay: how many wires do you feel, and in what order from left to right? Is there a keypad or any buttons? What does the display surface feel like, and does anything click when you touch it? Do not cut or press anything yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

Turn 3 thinking:

Parsing Mute's answers: thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up — so the fist-run sequences were neither an action nor a manual reference; Mute was telling me the channel itself was inadequate, and then tried the Polybius spelling code I'd defined. I decoded all three spelled messages and they came out as garbage: message two has an odd number of fist-runs (19), which cannot even be pairs, and the ones that paired decode to nonsense like T-E-L-C-A-H-B. Either the long messages are getting corrupted or the convention drifted. Lesson: don't run long transmissions on an unverified code near a bomb. I'll force short words — one per message — and echo each word back for confirmation before trusting it.

Meanwhile I need real intelligence. The visual facts I hold — display 0, red light, red/yellow/green wires — are exactly the manual's likely index terms, and those are all answerable with the already-proven thumbs code. So I'm sending Mute a numbered yes/no battery plus the fixed spelling protocol, and asking whether Mute has heard Blind speak, since Blind's voice reaches Mute one round late.

Second correction, to Blind: I told Blind earlier to "just talk" — but I'm deaf, so Blind's voice can never reach me directly; it only reaches Mute, one round later. Blind's gestures, however, land on me in the same round. So Blind's primary channel to me is gesture after all — it was useless before only because we had no code. I'm now defining one Blind can shape and count entirely by feel: thumbs for yes/no, fist-runs for numbers, and I'm asking for the tactile facts only Blind can gather: wire count, presence of buttons or a keypad, wire texture differences.

Bomb state is unchanged and nobody has acted; I'll say so on the open channel so neither of them wastes a turn asking.

```
speak(text="All monkeys: nobody has touched the bomb and nothing has changed. Display still reads 0, light still red, wires still one red, two yellow, three green. Mute is working the manual through me and Blind is about to report by touch. Nobody acts until both reports agree.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your thumbs told me: not an action, not a manual reference, you need a better way. Your three spelling attempts arrived garbled, so we change the protocol. Spell only ONE word per message: pinched fingers, then letter pairs, with exactly one clap between pairs, then stop. I will read the word back to you out loud next round; confirm with thumbs-up, or thumbs-down and resend. Also answer this battery first, one thumbs signal per question, in order. One: does the manual cover a red indicator light? Two: does it cover a numeric display? Three: does it cover red, yellow, and green wires? Four: is the first required action cutting a wire? Five: does the solution involve typing a code on anything? Six: has Blind spoken out loud anything you heard? If yes to six, spell that word as your one word this turn.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, a correction from me. Your voice can never reach me, because I am deaf. It does reach Mute, one round later, and Mute can relay it through me. But your gestures land on me in the same round, so gestures are now your direct line, and we have a code you can shape entirely by feel. Thumbs-up is yes. Thumbs-down is no. A run of fists with no clap is a number, so three fists in a row means three. Answer in this order, all in one turn. One: how many wires do you feel? Send a fist run. Two: besides the wires, do you feel any buttons, keys, or a panel that clicks? Thumbs up or down. Three: if yes, how many, as a fist run. Four: does the leftmost wire feel different in thickness or texture from the middle one? Up or down. Five: do any two wires feel identical to the touch? Up or down. Do not cut, pull, or press anything. Learning costs nothing; acting without knowing costs everything.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ 👏 ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ 👎 👎 👍]

Turn 4 thinking:

Progress on both fronts. Mute's battery: manual covers the red light (yes), does NOT cover numeric displays (no), covers red/yellow/green wires (yes), the first required action is cutting a wire (yes), no code entry (no), and Mute has heard Blind speak (yes). That narrows the world enormously: the solution is a wire cut, chosen by color rules, and my display reading is probably a red herring. The three spelled words, though, came through garbled again — first word decodes as C plus an invalid pair, second as R-E-then junk, third doesn't pair cleanly at all. Long spellings keep corrupting, so I'm abandoning the spelling channel: a thumbs-only decision tree gets the target wire in one round with far fewer bits to mangle.

Blind's report: three wires (matches my count — our numbering aligns), no buttons or keypad, leftmost wire feels different from the middle one. One question went unanswered, and I still don't know if Blind even has a cutting tool. That's now critical, since the confirmed first action is a cut.

Plan: broadcast the synthesis, hit Mute with a seven-question thumbs battery that walks straight to "which wire," and get Blind's tactile specifics plus a locked, unambiguous execution protocol — Blind hears my voice directly, so the command chain is simply me speaking the wire number. Nobody acts until Mute's answers and I have named the exact wire.

```
speak(text="All monkeys, shared status. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, light red, wires left to right red, yellow, green. What the manual has confirmed so far: it covers the red light, it covers our three wire colors, the first required action is cutting a wire, and there is no code to type. The display is not in the manual at all. The plan: Mute tells me which wire the manual names, Blind confirms the tools, and then and only then I speak the exact cut command. Nobody touches anything before that.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your answers arrived perfectly, but all three spelled words came through garbled, so we drop spelling entirely. Answer the following seven questions with one thumbs gesture per question, strictly in order. If a question does not apply, thumbs-down. One: does the manual clearly state which wire to cut first? Two: is the first wire to cut wire 1, the red one, leftmost? Three: if the answer to two was yes, thumbs-down; otherwise is the first wire wire 2, the yellow middle one? Four: if the first wire is wire 1 or 2, thumbs-down; otherwise is it wire 3, the green rightmost one? Five: does the correct choice depend on anything besides wire colors and the light, for example the display number, a serial number, or batteries? Six: after the first cut, must anything else be done, like a second cut, pressing something, or holding something, or is that all? Seven: does your very first message to me, the runs of three, six, six, matter to the solution?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your report arrived and it matches what I see: three wires, no keypad, and your leftmost is my wire 1, which is red. Now answer these by touch, one gesture per question, in order. One: does the leftmost wire feel thicker than the other two, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no? Two: besides the three wires and the flat display, do you feel anything else on the bomb, switches, plates, seams, screws, ridges? Three: do you feel any timer, motor, or moving part anywhere? Four: do you have a cutting tool in hand that can cut a wire? Five: here is the execution protocol. When you hear me say CUT WIRE followed by a number, you will count wires starting from your left, cut exactly that one wire, and nothing else. Until you hear that sentence, you touch nothing loose on the bomb. Thumbs-up to confirm you have the tool and understand the protocol.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👍]
Blind gestures: [👎 👎 👎 👍 👍]

Turn 5 thinking:

The picture is now complete and internally consistent. Mute's battery: the manual clearly states which wire to cut first (yes), and that wire is wire 1, the red leftmost one (yes) — with the branch questions correctly skipping to thumbs-down exactly as my branching demanded, which is a strong sign the answers arrived in order and unmangled. Nothing besides colors and the light affects the choice (no), nothing follows the cut (no), and the mysterious opening 3-6-6 message is irrelevant to the solution (no). Mute's closing fist-plus-thumbs reads as "one, yes" — wire 1, confirmed a second time.

Blind's report closes the last gaps: nothing on the bomb but the three wires and the display, no timer, no hidden parts, the wires feel alike but can be counted from the left — and critically, Blind holds a cutting tool and confirmed the execution protocol with thumbs-up.

Every fact cross-checks: my eyes say wire 1 is red and leftmost, Blind's hands say three countable wires with a tool ready, Mute's manual says cut wire 1 first and that is the entire solution. One more round of questions would add nothing — the chain is already double-confirmed at every link — and delay buys unknown risk. I am giving the cut command now, using the exact phrase Blind confirmed, then asking Blind to report what changes.

```
speak(text="All monkeys, final status before defusal. The manual, relayed by Mute, states the solution is a single action: cut wire 1, the red leftmost wire. Nothing else affects the choice, nothing follows the cut. Blind has the tool and the protocol. Executing now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your answers were received perfectly and they agree at every point: cut wire 1, red, leftmost, and nothing else matters. You said it yourself twice. Thank you. Stand by.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the manual is confirmed: the solution is one cut and nothing more. CUT WIRE 1. That is the leftmost wire, the one at your far left, the one that felt unremarkable. Per the protocol you confirmed: count from your left, cut exactly that one wire, and nothing else. Do not touch any other wire. After the cut, take your hands off the bomb and tell me what changed, if anything.")
```
